slides.headline:
Two national chains, combined,
made less profit than this one bakery.
slides.subline: Sungsimdang, 15 Daejong-ro 480beon-gil, Jung-gu, Daejeon — baking since 1956, listed as open year-round by Korea's national tourism office, and still refusing to sell anywhere but Daejeon

slides.label: Branches outside Daejeon, seventy years in. The Korea Herald reported in April 2024 that all 11 of Sungsimdang's branches sit in one city, and that the owning family has refused to expand elsewhere since 1956
slides.note: Sources: Korea Tourism Organization, official English site (english.visitkorea.or.kr) — address, phone, hours, open all year · The Korea Herald, 19 Apr 2024 — 11 branches all in Daejeon, no-expansion policy, 2023 revenue · Korean business press, 12 Apr 2026 — 2025 revenue and operating profit · Korean restaurant database — Daejeon Station branch shown trading on 9 Sep 2026

items.t: 262.9 billion won of revenue last year
items.d: Korean business media reported in April 2026 that Rosso, the company behind Sungsimdang, booked 262.9 billion won for 2025 — up 35.7% on 2024's 193.8 billion. In 2023 the figure was 124.3 billion

items.t: 64.3 billion won operating profit, a 24.4% margin
items.d: The same April 2026 reporting put Paris Baguette's operating profit at 26 billion won and Tous les Jours' at 28.2 billion. Together, 54.2 billion — under what one city's bakery made alone

items.t: 1,700 won for the bread doing the carrying
items.d: Twigim soboro, a deep-fried crumb bun, was still priced at 1,700 won in the 2026 reporting. The Korea Herald put cumulative sales past 96 million units as of 2023

slides.title:
The refusal is
the business model.
slides.body:
The origin was not a brand strategy. Korean and English accounts agree the founder's family fled Hungnam in December 1950, settled on Geoje, and in 1956 boarded a train for Seoul that broke down at Daejeon. A priest gave them two sacks of flour. They sold steamed buns outside the station and stayed.

Seventy years on, the staying is the strategy. Because it cannot be bought elsewhere, buying it means going there — and that is measurable. April 2026 coverage noted 49.31 million visitors to Daejeon's Jung-gu district in 2025, up 9.6%.

In 2024 the leverage was tested. Korail's retail arm sought around 440 million won a month for the station branch, against the 100 million being paid. After failed bidding rounds and loud public sympathy, the lease settled near 133 million from November 2024. The landlord blinked.
slides._note: the real message of this post

items.d: Korea's tourism office gives the phone as 1588-8069 and hours as 08:00-22:00, open all year round. Korean listings give 06:30-23:00 for the same address. The sources disagree, so confirm before you travel

items.t: Or catch it inside the station
items.d: A Korean restaurant database places the Daejeon Station branch on the 2nd floor of the station building, 215 Jungang-ro, Dong-gu, at 07:00-22:30, and showed it trading on 9 September 2026. Daejeon is roughly an hour from Seoul by KTX

items.t: What the queue is usually for
items.d: Twigim soboro at 1,700 won and leek bread at 2,000 won, per that database. The tourism office names fried soboro and pantalong leek bread as the specialities, out of a range it describes as close to 400 items

items.t: Seasonal cakes sell out, and resale is barred
items.d: Korean press in December 2025 described a 49,000-won strawberry siru cake sold only at the Cake Boutique store, with no online orders and queues reported over 200 metres. Purchase limits followed after resellers listed it near 140,000 won

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked on 9 September 2026.
slides.by:
Hours, prices and branch counts differ between the tourism office, Korean listings and press reports — worth re-checking on the day you go.
A bakery being remarkable as a business is not a verdict on how the bread tastes to you. That stays personal.
